objective: Stress the buffer-bound property at small boundary shapes and boundary shifts, always with P > W, to catch one-past-the-end or negative-index accesses that only occur at edges.
observation: For each boundary configuration, the post-run output guard-canary values and any target memory-fault or bounds-check report produced by that run.
pass_condition: Accept only if, for every configuration, no memory-fault or bounds-check report is emitted, both output guard canaries equal their baseline sentinel values, and at least one output-buffer slot differs from its sentinel initialization (proving the kernel executed for that shape). Reject on any fault/report or any changed canary in any configuration.
setup: On the target, build the unmodified candidate kernel and run a sweep over small shapes with padding, e.g., W in {1,2,3,16}, H in {1,2,3}, P = W + 3, and shiftX/shiftY in {0,1,W-1,W,W+1} plus -1 where representable, all satisfying the admitted domain. For each configuration, bracket the H*P output buffer with sentinel guard canaries, initialize every output slot to a distinct sentinel, fill the source with unique binary32 values none equal to the sentinel, and protect the pages around the W*H source region as in the runtime-observation plan. Run, synchronize, and record canaries and any fault/report for each configuration.
